subject.title: fix: stabilize OpenClaw beta setup and PT-PT formatting

question: Should the Windows Companion default to `2026.7.2-beta.3` before an unmodified official beta artifact contains the required upstream wizard-runtime correction and passes the real setup/reconnect path?
rationale: The branch intentionally selects a prerelease default, but the only successful final E2E evidence applies an unmerged upstream patch after installation; accepting that support contract is a release-policy choice rather than a mechanical downstream repair.

options.title: Wait for an official fixed artifact
options.body: Keep the PR open and do not make beta.3 the default until the upstream correction ships and the exact official artifact passes redacted setup/reconnect proof.

options.title: Approve a temporary prerelease default
options.body: Explicitly accept that fresh native setup may still fail on the official beta.3 artifact while relying on a later upstream release to close the gap.

options.title: Split the independent fixes
options.body: Land only the Companion fixes that do not change the default package, and defer the beta-target change to a separately proven update.

recommendation.title: Wait for an official fixed artifact
recommendation.body: Keep the PR open and do not make beta.3 the default until the upstream correction ships and the exact official artifact passes redacted setup/reconnect proof.

likelyOwner.reason: The supplied feature history ties the central setup-target and pipeline changes to CassieMei, making this the best available routing candidate for the release-boundary discussion.
